hook.line: The café is open, and Tomás and Vale are raising a glass. In Spanish a dream does not get achieved: it comes true, and it happens to you.
hook.es: Se nos cumplió el sueño de abrir el café.
hook.en: Our dream of opening the café came true.

examples.es: A Rosa se le cumplió el sueño de tener un café.
examples.en: Rosa's dream of having a café came true.

examples.es: Se me cumplió el sueño de vivir en Bogotá.
examples.en: My dream of living in Bogotá came true.

examples.es: Ojalá se te cumplan todos tus deseos.
examples.en: I hope all your wishes come true. (to a friend)

examples.es: A Tomás no se le cumplió el sueño de ser músico.
examples.en: Tomás's dream of being a musician did not come true.

rule:
Dreams and wishes are not things you do; they *come true*. So the dream is the subject: *el sueño se cumplió*. The person it happens to goes in front with *se* + *me / te / le / nos / les*: *se me cumplió el sueño*, my dream came true. The verb agrees with the dream: *se cumplieron mis sueños*.

Promises and your word are different: a person keeps them, so there is no *se*: *cumplió su promesa*, *cumplí mi palabra*.
smallPrint: Teachers call the *se le cumplió* kind of sentence an unplanned *se*: the event happens to the person rather than being done by them.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *me* or *le*, for my own dream: Se ___ cumplió el sueño de vivir en Bogotá. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Se me cumplió el sueño de vivir en Bogotá.
yourTurn.why: The dream belongs to me, so *me* goes after *se*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *cumplió* or *cumplieron*: Se ___ todos mis sueños. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: The verb agrees with the dreams, and there are many, so *cumplieron*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Hernando kept his promise.
yourTurn.why: A person keeps a promise with plain *cumplió*, no *se*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Our dream of opening the café came true.
yourTurn.answer: Se nos cumplió el sueño de abrir el café.
accept: El sueño de abrir el café se nos cumplió.
yourTurn.why: *Nos* says who it happened to, and *cumplió* agrees with one dream.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: I hope all your wishes come true.
yourTurn.answer: Ojalá se te cumplan todos tus deseos.
yourTurn.why: *Te* is you, and *cumplan* is plural because the wishes are plural.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *A Tomás se le cumplió el sueño de ser músico.*
yourTurn.answer: A Tomás no se le cumplió el sueño de ser músico.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about yourself: *Hernando cumplió su promesa.*
yourTurn.why: Now you are the one who keeps it, so *cumplí* and *mi*.

pitfalls.why: A dream does not do anything; it comes true by itself, and *se* says so.

pitfalls.wrong: Rosa se cumplió el sueño de tener un café.
pitfalls.right: A Rosa se le cumplió el sueño de tener un café.
pitfalls.why: Rosa is the person it happens to, so she comes in with *a* and *le*, not as the subject.
The verb agrees with the dreams, so many dreams need *cumplieron*.
